title: M0: Spike: the drum rack preset (.adg) anatomy, from files saved by the DAW
description:
## Purpose

Answer, with real files saved by the DAW, exactly what a drum rack preset (`.adg`) must contain for a kit to load with the right pads, pitches, levels and warping, before any spec or product code is written. The `.alc` clip format is owned by the sidecar initiative (apricitus-d7746d); this spike only confirms the parts the clip folder relies on (clip name, info text, region, file reference) and reuses that initiative's findings (its spike is apricitus-9fb5fe; the set export's is apricitus-f838a3) if they have already run.

## Questions the spike answers

1. Minimal preset: the root element's version attributes, the drum group device, one branch per pad, and which elements the DAW refuses to load without.
2. Pad notes: how a branch's receiving note is stored (plain MIDI note or an inverted value), and the default note for pad 1 (expected C1 = 36).
3. Sampler per pad: root key, transpose, detune (cents), volume (linear or dB), sample start/end (frames), playback mode (classic with note-off vs one-shot), release, loop off.
4. Warping inside the sampler: are warp markers written the same way as in a clip (seconds to beats), and which warp modes exist there.
5. File references: absolute path, relative path, or both; does the DAW relink by relative path when the preset sits in a user library folder; are size/CRC fields required.
6. Velocity: the sampler's velocity-to-volume setting that comes closest to Apricity's velocity curve (`velocity_db`, 100 = matched level, 127 about +4 dB, 40 about -16 dB).
7. Clip file (confirm only): clip name, info text, start/end/loop region, warp on/off for an unwarped sample.

## Artifact it leaves (no product code)

- `design/daw-presets.md`: an annotated minimal XML skeleton for the preset, the field-by-field mapping table (kit -> rack), the answers above, and a Mermaid diagram of the document tree.
- Reference files saved by the DAW under `crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/` (gzipped XML only, pointing at audio paths; no audio in git).

## Definition of Done

- Every question above has an answer backed by a reference file.
- The owner has decided the open questions recorded on the initiative (pad note layout, MIDI file vs MIDI clip, reference vs copy audio).
- Applies: design note (6), fixtures (5), running log (10). Specs, code, schema, CLI, docs, web: not applicable (spike).

## Dependencies

- Shares findings with the sidecar spike (apricitus-d7746d) and the set export (apricitus-6edba8); whichever runs first writes the shared file-reference and warp-marker sections.

comments.text:
## Where reference files come from (decided 2026-09-26, corrected)

Checked: the DAW is not installed on the owner's development Mac, and neither the persistent library (~5,500 files) nor the production bucket holds any `.als`, `.alc`, `.adg` or `.asd`. The owner does hold a paid Studio licence, installed on the studio machine. So:

1. **Reference files come from the owner's licensed install.** Its bundled Core Library ships thousands of `.adg`/`.alc` files and `.asd` sidecars beside its sample WAVs, and the owner's own sets supply `.als`. The spike's first task is a short list of exact paths and files to copy from the studio machine into a fixtures folder here (record each file's origin; never commit audio). Public git repositories are a supplement for older-version examples only.
2. **Test material.** Every test and conformance check runs against samples and manifests from the production library (sync it down read-only; never push). Pick a fixed, named handful for determinism.
3. **Acceptance.** Opening an export in the DAW happens on the studio machine, or on this Mac if the owner installs the licensed copy here. Acceptance tasks stay blocked, not skipped, until then; the machine-checkable conformance tests are the gate.

comments.text:
## Spike summary (Spike Drum Rack Presets, 2026-09-26)

**Answered from DAW-saved files (provisional: other people's 12.2/12.3 installs, MIT):**
- Q2: ReceivingNote is stored as 128 - note; pad 1 (C1 = 36) = 92; SendingNote always 60.
- Q3: Simpler RootKey always 60; transpose = Pitch/TransposeKey (st, -48..48), detune = Pitch/TransposeFine (ct, -50..50); VolumeAndPan/Volume in dB (-36..36), sample gain linear; SampleStart/End in frames at the file's rate (end = frames - 1); PlaybackMode 0 classic / 1 one-shot / 2 slicing; ReleaseTime ms.
- Q4: sampler warp markers are the same WarpMarker SecTime/BeatTime as a clip's, whole-file, with a hidden trailing marker +1/32 beat; warp modes 0 Beats, 1 Tones, 2 Texture, 3 Re-Pitch, 4 Complex, 6 Complex Pro.
- Q5 (partly): FileRef anatomy and the RelativePathType table (0/1/3/5/6/7); the DAW always writes Path + RelativePath + size + 16-bit CRC.

**Unknown until the DAW runs:** Q1 minimal element set; Q5 relinking by relative path and whether size/CRC may be 0; Q6 the DAW's velocity curve (provisional fit: Vel 0.60, Volume -8.2 dB, within 2.3 dB of velocity_db for 40..127); Q7 .alc (no public clip file exists).

**Waits on the DAW:** apricitus-d577ee (owner saves kit-reference.adg, the note variant, clip-warped/unwarped.alc) and apricitus-661b66 (owner loads the 3 candidates, velocity measurement). Both left in_progress; apricitus-f2d6c6 done, left open for review. Owner checklist and re-check paths are in the note.

**Files created:**
- design/daw-presets.md
- crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/presets/README.md
- DAW-saved (MIT): daw-12.3-drum-sampler-kit.adg, daw-12.3-simpler-kit-64.adg, daw-12.3-simpler-warped.adv, daw-12.2-sliced-racks.als
- spike-written: candidate-full-kit.adg, candidate-trimmed-kit-v12.adg, candidate-trimmed-kit-v11.adg

**Notes for review:** the DAW-saved fixtures and the candidates necessarily contain the vendor's name inside the gzipped XML (it is the root element); no text I wrote spells it. design/vocabulary.md was not edited (rows drafted in Decision 16). Shared findings for apricitus-f838a3 and apricitus-9fb5fe are in the note's 'Shared findings'.
